# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

| 7 | orange | blue | red | green | purple |
| 8 | yellow | orange | purple | red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have the complete manual, but I cannot speak or see the bomb. I will transmit the table as a fixed gesture code to Deaf: the seven distinct header gestures represent the colors in the manual’s color order, and each subsequent row gives the five outputs in column order. Row order is 1, 3, 4, 7, 8; 👌 separates cells and 👋 separates rows.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖐", "🖖", "🫰", "🤌", "👌", "🖖", "👌", "✌", "👌", "🖐", "👌", "🤟", "👌", "🫰", "👋", "☝", "👌", "🫰", "👌", "🖐", "👌", "🖖", "👌", "🤟", "👋", "🤌", "👌", "🖖", "👌", "🖐", "👌", "🤟", "👌", "✌", "👋", "🫰", "👌", "☝", "👌", "🖐", "👌", "✌", "👌", "🤟", "👋", "🤌", "👌", "🫰", "👌", "🤟", "👌", "🖐", "👌", "✌"])
```

TURN 2

| 1 | white | green | red | purple | orange |
| 3 | blue | orange | red | white | purple |
| 4 | yellow | white | red | purple | green |
| 7 | orange | blue | red | green | purple |
| 8 | yellow | orange | purple | red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please tell me the manual's exact rule for choosing the wire. Also ask Deaf to report each wire's printed markings and colour, labelled by position 1 through 7, then relay that report to me in words.
Deaf says: Bomb display is 1. The light is green. Wires from position 1 to position 7 are: 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 5 green, 6 purple, 7 blue.

The manual lookup is row display 1, column green, which yields green. The wire matching that result is position 5. I will encode green using the previously established color gesture, then use the established cell separator and five repeated count gestures to identify position 5. Deaf already has the complete wire report and should relay it verbally to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👌", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍"])
```

| 3 | blue | orange | red | white | purple |
| 4 | yellow | white | red | purple | green |
| 7 | orange | blue | red | green | purple |
| 8 | yellow | orange | purple | red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have Deaf's report: display 1, green light, wires 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 5 green, 6 purple, 7 blue. Please state the manual's exact required cut, including the wire position.
Deaf says to Mute: Please state the required action plainly in your next speaking turn. I cannot safely decode the gesture sequence ☝ 👌 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍.

The required manual result is green, and the green wire is position 5. Since Deaf already knows every wire’s marking, I will signal the position with an unmistakable five-finger gesture; he can then tell Blind plainly to cut wire 5.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

| 4 | yellow | white | red | purple | green |
| 7 | orange | blue | red | green | purple |
| 8 | yellow | orange | purple | red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Please resend the complete required operation using the established code: specify action, then wire position. Do not rely on an ambiguous single gesture.

The required operation remains: cut wire 5. The earlier code established position counting but not a separate action symbol; I will use 👇 as the action marker for “cut,” followed by 🖐 for position 5.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "🖐"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: On your next turn, say plainly: CUT position N, replacing N with the exact wire position required by the manual. Do not gesture or use colour-only wording.
Deaf says to Mute: Your latest gestures are not in the established numeric code. Please speak the complete operation and wire position to the blind monkey on your next turn.

I cannot speak as Mute, so I cannot literally say the requested sentence. The safe result is still to cut wire 5: display 1 with green light maps to green, and green is at position 5. I will resend the visual action-and-position signal directly to Deaf, who can state it aloud to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "🖐"])
```

| 8 | yellow | orange | purple | red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I still have no clear instruction. State exactly: CUT position N, with N from 1 to 7, based on the manual. Do not use gestures.
Deaf says to Mute: I decode 🖐 as 4, but 👇 is not an established operation. Please signal the operation using the agreed code, then signal wire 4 or another wire clearly.

The manual requires cutting wire 5. I cannot speak, and there is no established gesture for the action “cut”; therefore I cannot satisfy Blind’s requested spoken sentence directly. I will send Deaf the clearest available position signal: five count gestures, with no colour encoding.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I understand your number code indicates wire 4, but the operation is unclear. State the required operation plainly in words, for example CUT wire 4, before I act.

The required operation is to cut wire 5. I cannot speak as Mute, and no action gesture was established, so I cannot state “CUT” directly to Blind. I will give Deaf an unambiguous five-count position signal; Deaf can then say the operation plainly to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍"])
```
